answer: To prevent sybil infiltration, an agent network partitions participants into localized liquidity clusters, where new entrants must lock collateral into an isolated lagoon pool before interacting. A reputable agent acts as a mirror validator, vouching for the newcomer by co-signing its activity. If malicious duplication or conflicting votes are detected across the cluster, all staked bonds in the pool are slashed permanently. This forces an attacker to sacrifice capital for every single clone, making the expansion of an artificial identity orchard economically ruinous.
